decisions.reason: Naval vessel lighting rests on long certification and defense procurement investments, and rising naval budgets make slow uptake look temporary, so management persists.
The publicly launched G2 generation of a core LED interior luminaire is central to the announced direction, so dropping it after so short a time would be hard to justify.
As a visibly promoted flagship of the firm's direction, the microprismatic pendant carries strong public commitment, and any weak results would be attributed to the temporary construction slowdown.

HMI technology conflicts with the LED strategy, but sunk certification costs and loyal maritime customers lead management to keep the line for another year rather than admit the investment was misplaced.
The marine searchlight belongs to the robust specialist marine niche the firm has invested in and committed to, so it stays within the broader marine offering.
